question: Should `/status` show exact cumulative transcript-backed session cost, and if so must the implementation preserve the default fast status path with a bounded or maintained aggregate?
rationale: The user value is clear, but the active fix has a maintainer-visible availability tradeoff around exact cost reads versus status responsiveness.

options.title: Show cost with a bounded aggregate
options.body: Proceed with this feature only if the implementation avoids full transcript scans on ordinary status paths, using persisted, maintained, or bounded cost data.

options.title: Accept exact full-scan cost
options.body: Allow exact cumulative transcript reads in status output and explicitly own the possible slowdown for very large sessions.

options.title: Defer status cost
options.body: Keep cost available through usage APIs or future aggregate storage work instead of adding it to status now.

recommendation.title: Show cost with a bounded aggregate
recommendation.body: Proceed with this feature only if the implementation avoids full transcript scans on ordinary status paths, using persisted, maintained, or bounded cost data.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent status path history and the performance/product tradeoff make steipete the best available routing owner from the observed history.
